items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: copying a little bit of Frenchmaster Debussy, you know Debussy... you figured you'd better do a little Debussy, use a little augmented chords in there.

ctx.x: I don't know where he was. He played Evansville, Indiana wasn't he? Someplace in Indiana. Someplace in Indiana. He's better played trombone.

Uh, Reeves. Reeves, Reeves, sure. Reuben Reeves. Reuben Reeves, that's it, Reuben Reeves. Well I made the first arrangements for them to record. They recorded for Brunswick Records I think. Some old arrangement. they started using the augmented chord, copying a little bit of Frenchmaster Debussy, you know Debussy. And so that was the first time I used the consecutive augmented chords that, you know, you heard so much about it and you figured you'd better do a little Debussy, use a little augmented chords in…
Yes, part of Peyton's band, but Ruben got them. Did you record with them?
